elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 4.3: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall ..." — covers both triggers.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 4.3(a): "at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 4.3(b): "within thirty (30) days, return to the Company all Content, user information and customer and order data", running from the opening "Upon expiration or termination" trigger.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: 4.3(c): "thereafter delete Company Data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing" — sequenced after the return obligation in (b).

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same 4.3 lead-in: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 4.3(a) grants assistance for up to six (6) months, which encompasses at least 90 days of availability at Company's request.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 4.3(b) requires return of all Company Data within thirty (30) days of expiration or termination in machine-readable form.

reasons: The inserted Section 4.3 is a single concise paragraph that tracks the playbook's model language and satisfies every preferred element (six-month assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion thereafter); the fallback is satisfied a fortiori.

Minimality holds: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added damages, indemnity or procedural mechanics, and no change to Section 4.1's term/notice construct or the Termination Payment schedule in 4.2(c).

Intent is preserved: the defined term "Company Data" is created in-line at 4.3(b), existing cross-references are untouched, and no retained sentence is contradicted. Section 10.7's survival list is an affirmative enumeration rather than an exclusive "only these sections survive" statement, and 4.3 is by its own terms a post-termination obligation, so the omission of 4.3 from 10.7 is a drafting nicety rather than a defect requiring repair; the drafter may optionally note it in the comment without expanding the redline.
Party direction is correct throughout: HDI (Vendor/Host) owes the obligations and the Company (Customer) receives the data and assistance on request.
